topic: How does the hybrid SIW-waveguide feeding topology balance efficiency and compactness in V-band satellite antenna designs?
consensus_response: The hybrid SIW-waveguide feeding topology balances efficiency and compactness in V-band satellite antenna designs by minimizing feeder line loss through the use of EBG structures, advanced simulations, and phased arrays and FSS. Additionally, improving material properties accuracy during the design stage is crucial to refining the design and reducing discrepancies between simulations and measurements. This balanced approach enables the creation of more efficient and compact V-band satellite antenna designs.
reference_context: A wideband high-gain high-efficiency hybrid integrated plate array antenna for V-band inter-satellite links was presented, consisting of microstrip patches, substrate integrated waveguide (SIW), and waveguide power dividers. The radiation efficiency of SIW arrays with different sizes was compared by experiment, and the hybrid SIW-waveguide feeding topology was optimized to realize high efficiency, low cost, and compact configuration at the same time.
